data.title: Pathpulse.ai

children.text: Cities lose $1 trillion a year to traffic congestion.
PathPulse.ai

is building the infrastructure layer to change that — a decentralised mobility intelligence network where every driver with a smartphone becomes a live data node. Their Scout app captures 60+ types of road conditions via computer vision, turning crowdsourced driving footage into structured intelligence for governments, mapping platforms, and logistics operators. The platform sits at the intersection of big data, computer vision, and smart city infrastructure — backed by $900K in pre-seed funding and already live in South Africa with 35,000+ registered contributors. 

I designed the client-side dashboard that makes all of that data readable — giving government officials and urban planners a clear, actionable view of what's happening across their regions.

data.keywords: AI, GovTech, IoT, Big Data, B2B SaaS, Decentralised Network, Client-side Analytics Data, Dashboard

data.title: Roadlyne

children.text: India's logistics industry loses over ₹1.5 lakh crore a year to inefficiency — idle trucks, fuel theft, unmonitored drivers, and zero real-time visibility across fleets.
Roadlyne

is building the operational backbone to fix that — an all-in-one fleet and transport management platform where GPS hardware, real-time telematics, and logistics software come together in a single system. Fleet owners can track every truck live, monitor driver behaviour, manage geofences, and control expenses. Transport operators can run the full trip lifecycle — from booking and dispatch to delivery confirmation — without a single phone call or WhatsApp message. The platform is built to scale from 5 trucks to 500+, with 99.9% uptime and multi-platform connectivity across mobile, tablet, and web — operating in a market where the leading players manage 2M+ trucks across 1,600+ cities in India.

I designed the end-to-end web app product for both Roadlyne Fleet and Roadlyne Transport — transforming a mobile-only experience into a fully responsive web platform across 100+ screens, giving fleet owners and transport operators a clear, actionable view of their entire operation from any device.

data.keywords: B2B SaaS, Product Design, Fleet Management, Web app, Responsive Design, Real Time Data, Design System

children.text: I grew up in a house where books lived everywhere: on the dining table, the kitchen counter, the stairs, even in the car. My dad teaches Maths, my mom teaches Physics, and curiosity wasn’t optional. It was just the air we breathed.

Maybe that’s why I scored 100 in Maths until 9th standard and stood first at my centre in the 12th boards, and still somehow became a designer. I don’t think the two are that different. Both are about finding the most elegant solution to a hard problem.
I studied IT Engineering with a major in Cyber Security, and for our final-year project, my team and I built
CAP (Central Assessment Program)

, a system to modernise how institutions run exams and evaluations. It earned us a patent, which still feels a little surreal to say. I loved the logic, but there was always another side of me: watercolours since childhood, and a camera in my hand the moment I step outside. I shoot street photography and dump it on
VSCO
every other day, like a journal. Design was where both halves finally made sense together.
Today, I’m 24 and the Creative Director at
Not on Sunday Studios

in Kolhapur, and I’m loving it. I recently gave my GRE, and I still get humbled by what the great watercolourists did with just water and pigment. That feeling of knowing how much there is left to learn is probably the most useful thing I bring to my work.

Outside work, I’m happiest with a bike, an open road, and a few hours away from everything, whether I’m discovering somewhere new or just riding with people who make the journey worth it. I value the little things: conversations that run longer than planned, time together without a reason, and memories that don’t look like much at the time but stay for years.

That’s what I love about building Not on Sunday with the Fourman Studios team. It’s the easy back-and-forth, the shared thrill when an idea finally clicks, and having someone beside you who’s putting in the same effort.
Somewhere along the way, coworkers became people I genuinely care about, and work became something we’re building together. I hope we never lose that.
नमस्ते,
Amartya Katge
here,

I’ve always been curious about why people do what they do. Why one brand feels like home and another feels like a stranger. Why some ideas land instantly while others never quite click. I never got over those questions, and somewhere along the way, they became my job.

I’m a designer and Creative Director at Not On Sunday, working across brand, product, and digital experiences. Most of it comes down to understanding how people actually think and behave, then building around that instead of what we assume.
Based in India, and I work with founders, teams, and businesses who have a big, messy idea and need it to make sense to someone else.
